_comment: GCB-029 - EPIC TKT-018 Measurement Epoch Story 2, per TKT-000. Physical validation of the GCB-028 pipeline response: gcb_max_reduce with REG_STAGES=2 through the EXACT same ORFS/ASAP7 flow as GCB-027 (1 ns target, default recipe, no tuning). Only config diff vs GCB-027: VERILOG_TOP_PARAMS = REG_STAGES 2. Raw measurement, not a signed-off result.
params: WIDTH=16 N_ELEMENTS=64 MODE=MAX OUTPUT=BOTH SIGNED_CMP=1 TIE_LOW=1 REG_STAGES=2 (GCB-028: 2 OUTPUT pipeline stages after the tournament tree)

flow.identical_to: GCB-027 (same sv2v netlist, same constraint.sdc @ 1000 ps, same CORE_UTILIZATION=40 / PLACE_DENSITY=0.55, same platform asap7, default recipe, no tuning)
flow.only_diff: VERILOG_TOP_PARAMS = REG_STAGES 2  (ORFS chparam -set REG_STAGES 2 gcb_max_reduce before synth)

synth_sequential_area_um2.note: 46x DFFASRHQNx1 - the 2 output pipe stages of the WIDTH-16 value + 6-bit index; 2.81% of chip area

critical_path.worst_path_type: input -> output, COMBINATIONAL (Startpoint: a data input; Endpoint: max_val[*]) - same as GCB-027, still 22 violating paths
critical_path.wns_segment: the input -> val_pipe[0] segment (inputs into the first pipeline register) still carries ~1.44 ns of the tournament cone; +223 ps of headroom came from resizing + the shorter net loads once the cone terminates at a register instead of a top-level port
critical_path.new_register_paths: yes - val_pipe[0][b] -> val_pipe[1][b] (stage0->stage1, pure flop-to-flop, no logic between): reported slack (MET) +29.98 ps; vld_pipe[1] -> out_valid (vclk): MET; rst_n -> vld_pipe async removal: MET (+178 ps). None of the new register paths violate.
critical_path.verdict: The 2 stages are an OUTPUT pipeline (after the tree, per TKT-016's REG_STAGES). They did NOT split the ~1.67 ns combinational cone - they moved its endpoint from a port to a flop. Default ORFS synth does not run register retiming, so the promised 'retiming distributes the registers into the tree' did not happen. Result: -34% WNS/TNS, -19% power, +0.4% area, but timing NOT closed at 1 ns.

orange_verdict: Measured transfer function: +2 OUTPUT pipeline stages -> WNS -665 ps -> -442 ps (+34%), TNS -34%, power -19%, area +0.4% / +46 flops, congestion/DRC unchanged (0). Timing NOT closed - the reduce tree itself is still a ~1.44 ns single-segment cone. To break it needs registers INTERSPERSED in the tree levels (retiming enabled, or a mid-tree REG_STAGES placement), more stages, or the 4-ary variant. This falsifies the assumption that REG_STAGES=2 alone closes 1 ns.
